records.for_john: An older report the entry missed, and a press-only one, so it is not mine to act on. The KHL Foundation's release of 2026-09-30 (Madrid), reported by Fight Aging! on 2026-10-07, says that on 2026-03-11 a named person, one of 'a small number of people', was given an eleven-gene therapy that includes three of the cell-resetting genes (OCT4, SOX2 and KLF4), injected under a mucous membrane and switched on with doxycycline, in a project of Triple Helix Science led by a named doctor. The release names no registered trial and no registry number, reports no result, and says the foundation is still checking whether it was the first such dose anywhere. It does not meet this entry's test, which asks for a registered trial, so no stage would change. The change I would have made is a sentence in the notes saying that a dose outside any trial is claimed three months before the trial's first dose of 2026-06-09, and a check that the description's sentence about the genes having been tried only in animals until 2026 still reads correctly beside it. Both dates are before this week's window. Opened: the foundation's release, the Fight Aging! post and the trial's registry entry. Not opened: Triple Helix Science's own site.

records.found: The two web searches returned nothing dated in the window: the company's interim eye-trial results of 2026-10-08, which the record already describes, and a Neuron paper reported in February 2026 in which resetting memory-holding nerve cells restored memory in old mice. Two peer-reviewed mouse papers dated in the window were found another way, by a date-limited query to the Europe PMC literature database, which the procedure does not name as a way of finding papers; on the web searches alone this item would be quiet. Meiners and colleagues (Aging, 2026-10-27) reanalysed existing gene-activity data from the liver, kidney and spleen of old mice after seven months of cyclic resetting: age-related inflammation fell in liver and kidney, and the spleen showed signs of sustained growth stress that the authors call a possible risk. Mallavibarrena and colleagues (Aging Cell, dated 2026-11-01) report that old mice given cyclic resetting had less brain damage and better movement scores 48 hours after a stroke than untreated mice. Both are animal results on a rung the treatment already holds, and neither is a result in a person, so nothing moves. The records were searched for both first authors and both paper identifiers and hold neither.
records.found_outside_procedure: One query to Europe PMC limited to first publication dates 2026-10-25 to 2026-11-01 (terms: partial reprogramming, chemical reprogramming, epigenetic editing, epigenome editing; 23 results). The existing procedure names Europe PMC only for opening a known paper. Count this item as quiet if the trial scores only what the named web searches found.
